chapter_title: Concerning the Five Wonders that the Light Mind shall display in the Elect
chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by late institutional/paraenetic material: a virtue-list for the Elect (wisdom/faith/peace/love) and explicit church discipline (legal excommunication). Although it uses Manichaean cosmological terms (Light Mind), the language consistently maps the teaching onto community practice (preaching, assembly, brethren, church), rather than giving an internal cosmos→cosmos correspondential exposition. No recoverable pre-compilation correspondential substrate is present as a separable block.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic hagiographic attribution (“Once again the apostle speaks”) marks the editorial dialogue frame; even the remaining sentence functions as a chapter heading for community instruction about the Elect.
Institutional virtue list oriented to the Elect’s preaching (“shall preach and proclaim”)—a community-facing program rather than impersonal cosmological mechanics.
Continues the paraenetic/institutional logic: preaching → hearers → belief. No internal cosmological mapping; focused on communal reception.
Despite the “third” enumerator, the content is explicitly social (“assembly of his brethren”) and pastoral in aim (peace of heart), not a cosmic-degree correspondence.
Love is defined by relation to “brothers and sisters … seated [before] him,” i.e., liturgical/community setting—an application layer rather than substrate description.
Explicit church discipline (“legal excommunication,” “found in the church”) is institutional material; this is a clear late pastoral layer.

Uses a Manichaean cosmic agent (“Light Mind”) but applies it directly to forming the “new man” and validating the preceding virtue-program (“these five signs”); no autonomous, impersonal cosmological-correspondential exposition is developed.
Beatitude-style exhortation (“Blessed is every one…”) aimed at diligence in wisdom; paraenetic voice, not system-description.

Metaphors “faultless vessel” and especially “pearl without price” strongly echo NT/Gospel imagery (pearl of great price). Even without an explicit citation formula, the phrasing likely entered through Christian scriptural tradition rather than the older correspondential substrate.
